body:
Hard rule 6 sends dependency/licence changes to the operator, and the
documented procedure is "demote to defer, write `notes/dep-review-<PR>.md`".
There is no step that actually *delivers* the request to anyone. Writing the
note and restating the hold on the thread is the whole mechanism.

So "escalated" in the tick log means "a file was written". The operator is
never paged, and nothing re-raises the hold as it ages.

## Measured 2026-08-13

PR #1442 was held on 2026-08-08 (`fork-pr-1442-HELD-rule6`), CI green 8/8.
`notes/dep-review-1442.md` says "Operator decision required". The tick logs
say escalated on 08-08 and re-escalated on 08-13T06:46.

No ntfy of any kind had been sent since **2026-07-19** — grepping
`state/completed.log` for delivery rows shows the July escalations recorded
an explicit `HTTP 200`, and nothing for #1442. The hold sat 5 days. Two
contributors were blocked; one asked three times; a third party joined to ask
who the decision-maker even was.

This tick sent the ping by hand (`--tier needs-you`, HTTP 200) and it should
have gone out on 08-08.

## Why it persists

A hold with no expiry is indistinguishable from a decision to do nothing, and
the tick that inherits it sees a note file that reads as "handled". Each
subsequent tick then re-states the hold to the contributor rather than
questioning whether anyone was ever asked — which is what happened on 08-09
and again on 08-13.

## Fix

Two parts, both small:

1. The hold path must send the ntfy at the moment the hold is created, and log
   the delivery result (`HTTP 200`) alongside the hold row, so "escalated" is
   falsifiable from the ledger.
2. Holds need an expiry: a sweep that re-pings any `dep-review-*.md` whose PR
   is still open past a threshold, on the monotonic since-anchor pattern
   already used for the quiet-hold fix (46ac4e5). Without it the first ping
   failing silently reproduces the same five-day gap.

Related: F-8d8c15 (the follow-up board cannot see PRs, so a contributor
blocked behind a hold is also invisible to the board).
title: A rule-6 hold has no delivery step, so the escalation never reaches the operator
